unit.title: Создаём окно игры и первый игровой цикл

learning_outcomes.statement: Creates the first Pygame window with `display.set_mode()` and writes the first hand-rolled game loop: event pump, `display.flip()`, `clock.tick(60)`, and `screen.fill()` for frame clearing.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Creates the first Pygame window with `display.set_mode()` and writes the first hand-rolled game loop: event pump, `display.flip()`, `clock.tick(60)`, and `screen.fill()` for frame clearing.

`pygame.display.set_mode((600, 400))` returns a Surface that can be filled and read back. -- Confirmed -- under xvfb, `screen.fill((20,20,40)); screen.get_at((0,0))` returns `Color(20, 20, 40, 255)`, reproducing the notebook transcript exactly.

Unlike Tkinter's `mainloop()`, the Pygame loop is written by hand, giving per-frame control. -- Confirmed -- chapters 16-18 teach `root.mainloop()`; the contrast is accurate and pedagogically load-bearing.

Without handling `pygame.QUIT` the window stops responding. -- Confirmed as a correct description of OS behaviour; consistent with the 20.14 debug callout on the unread event queue, which is the mechanism.

`screen.fill(colour)` must run first each frame or previous frames leave trails. -- Confirmed -- reproduced deliberately by the screenshot generator's `scene_bug_bez_fill()`, whose output debug-missing-fill-trail.png shows the real trail.
